inventory.first_words_or_objects: On a donc le diagramme d'inclusions
Outlined left oval; middle downward triangle; filled right point; continuous slightly rising line. Labels are the immediately following inclusion chain.
Ceci n'implique pas que les quatre ensembles ... non parallèles.
Je me propose d'étudier les ensembles ... non parallèles.
Voici une façon très générale d'en obtenir des floppées.

notes.text: The page continues an argument about the relation Sigma1-minus intersect Sigma2-minus being nonempty and concludes that the two positive labels are uniquely determined. The author explicitly includes the E1 = E2 = empty-set case. This is a source account; no proof verification was performed.

An inclusion chain is followed by a drawn segment with three marked positions and a second copy of the chain below it. The hook directions were read individually from the ink. The NB gives the two amalgamation formulas with E2 below the first amalgamation sign and E1 below the second.

The slanted addition opens “Ceci n'implique pas que les quatre ensembles ... soient distincts”. It writes the cross equality Sigma1-plus = Sigma2-minus, uses the words “qui équivaut à”, and continues with E1 = Sigma12 and E2 = empty set. These are transcribed source claims, with no independent theorem asserted.

The explanatory parenthesis contains X minus Sigma1-plus and a final Sigma with a visible left-pointing over-arrow, a lower 1, and the high minus-comma-oval group. The ambiguous oval is retained as circle/zero. The small point above an earlier minus remains unresolved because the nearby line may own it.

The author says “On ne veut pas exclure ce cas, i.e.” and then discusses four distinct sets and the wording “non parallèles”. The last part is heavily revised: ens. is crossed, “deux décomp. bin.” is interlinear, and the adjacent qualification is cancelled. Its original wording and the live/cancelled state of the earlier sont remain uncertain.

The main lower paragraph begins “Je me propose d'étudier les ensembles finis ...”. The finite indexed-family description has a crossed initial capital, a live pi/Pi family, a cancelled right-hand expression, and a separate cancelled partial definition with epsilon. All legible pieces are retained. The last sentence introduces a “façon très générale” and ends with the stroke-led reading floppées/floppés.

No date or title is visible on this page. The small pale 26 at the lower left is recorded as archive sheet numbering under the supplied convention. No authorial proof-check annotation was observed on this page.

Mathematical and grammatical cues used only to assess letter candidates: the sentence before si suggests the expansion même for the written equals sign; ni ... mais supports non pas as an alternative; the adjoining Sigma1 labels support 1 in the doubtful pair; the live alpha in A supports the cancelled index statement. The visible signs, unresolved alternatives and cancellation states were retained without correcting the author's formulas.

notation.observation: Angular capitals with level top and foot; 12 occupies one lower level. Upper + and - are separate marks. The pair index in the slanted parenthesis retains a 1/t ambiguity at its first occurrence.
The empty-set sign is a narrow loop crossed by a long rising diagonal. It occurs in the opening relation, E1 = E2 = empty set, and the slanted E2 formula.
Each chain arrow has a visible head and a rounded tail-return; arrows point away from E1 and E2 in both copies.
Two short uprights on a base; the lower E index changes from 2 in the first NB row to 1 in the second.
A short left-pointing arrow is distinctly above the Sigma; a separate hollow oval follows a comma in the superscript. The oval still admits circle/zero.

The live family sign has one horizontal bar and two straight short legs. Size relative to Sigma favours lowercase pi, while the handwritten shape permits capital Pi. First live occurrence is marked; the later cancelled definition uses the first reading.
The high symbol in the cancelled partial definition has two open lobes, agreeing with epsilon rather than a plus sign.

The physical left mark has a pale oval centre; the central mark has a triangular downward foot; the right mark is filled and rounded. The TikZ reproduction follows those contours without inferring different abstract vertex types.
Before si there are two written horizontal strokes. The sign is retained literally; no handwritten letters spelling même were observed there.
